issues.problem: Context 3 (lying long enough means you will eventually give yourself away) fit 化けの皮が剥がれる from the same set just as well.
issues.action: Rewrote it so the giveaway is a slip, a story that stops adding up (辻褄が合わなくなって), which points to 尻尾を出す.

issues.problem: reg was formal, but the card itself has a casual spoken command (肝に銘じておけ from a shop manager). The phrase is serious in tone but is used across registers. Context 1's English added 'sir', a gender the Japanese does not give.
issues.action: Changed reg to neutral; removed 'sir' from the translation.

issues.problem: Misuse 1 (he is so unflappable he does not study the day before the exam) is a line natives say ironically, so it is not clearly wrong.
issues.action: Replaced it with a clear misuse: using it of a steady, heavy bookcase. The phrase is only said of people.

issues.problem: Misuse 1 (amazed by a friend's small fringe trim) is hyperbole that people use jokingly, so it is not clearly wrong.
issues.action: Replaced it with a clear grammar error: the amazed person as active subject (私は彼のマジックに度肝を抜いた); this needs the passive 度肝を抜かれた.

issues.problem: 'how' called it intransitive, but it is a を-verb. Misuse 1 (襟を正して studying for an exam) is defensible, since dictionaries also give the sense of approaching a task with a serious attitude.
issues.action: Changed 'how' to 'predicate ... and no other object'. Replaced the misuse with dressing up stylishly for a party, which the phrase never means.

issues.problem: Story check: all ten stories are null. None of these body-part or object idioms has a documented origin story. The fox/tanuki image in 尻尾を出す and 尻尾をつかむ is the usual dictionary explanation and stays in lit only.
issues.action: Kept stories null. Checked furigana, readings, near-synonym differences and cues; no other changes.
